executive_summary: US stock futures surged Monday as a fragile US-Iran ceasefire pause sent oil crashing 5-7%, lifting the S&P 500 futures +0.82%, Nasdaq +1.38%, and Dow +0.80%. The oil collapse eases immediate inflation pressure ahead of the FOMC decision Wednesday, where the Fed is expected to hold rates steady but markets price a 38% chance of a hike. This week brings the heaviest earnings calendar of the quarter: Microsoft and Meta report Wednesday, Apple and Amazon Thursday, with AI capital expenditure discipline the central question after Alphabet's capex shock triggered a 7% selloff. The VIX dropped 4.5% to 17.74, signaling markets are tentatively positioning for a risk-on week.

macro_events.title: US-Iran Ceasefire Pause — Oil Crashes 5-7%
macro_events.causal_chain: US and Iran pause strikes for 3rd consecutive night → Strait of Hormuz shipping risk eases (21% of global oil, 20% of LNG transits) → war-risk insurance premiums on VLCCs begin normalizing → Brent crashes 7.4% to ~$86/bbl, WTI -5.6% to ~$84 → Asian refiners no longer rerouting via Cape of Good Hope (saving $2M/trip, 12-14 days) → global energy supply chain de-risks → inflation expectations ease → 10Y yield slides 2bps to 4.68% → equity risk premium contracts → S&P futures +0.82%, VIX -4.5% to 17.74 → defense stocks lose war premium, airlines/transports rally on fuel cost relief
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East → Global oil trade → US/EU/Asia equity markets
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq drone attack — Brent +15% in 24h, then reversed 80% of move within 2 weeks as supply restored. Current reverse: oil was elevated at ~$92-100, ceasefire producing mirror-image unwind.
macro_events.counterargument: Ceasefire is extremely fragile — no formal agreement, just mutual restraint. Trump threatened stepped-up attacks last week. Any single strike restarts the cycle, snapping oil back above $100.

macro_events.title: FOMC Decision Wednesday — Hold Expected, Hike Not Off Table
macro_events.causal_chain: FOMC meets July 28-29, decision at 2pm ET Wednesday → Oil spike had pushed rate hike odds to 38% (up from 12% a week ago) → overnight oil crash may relieve hawkish pressure → Fed Chair Warsh pledged 2% inflation target but offered few forward clues → June CPI: headline -0.4% MoM but still 3.5% YoY, core 2.6% YoY → if dovish hold, equities extend rally, 10Y drops toward 4.50%, growth stocks lead → if hawkish hold with hike signal, 10Y spikes above 4.80%, tech sells off 3-5%
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US monetary policy → Global rate expectations, DXY, EM currencies
macro_events.historical_analog: June 2023 skip — Fed held but signaled more hikes coming; markets initially rallied, then sold off 4% over next two weeks.
macro_events.counterargument: Core CPI at 2.6% YoY is approaching the 2% target. With oil now crashing, headline inflation may undershoot significantly. Fed may signal patience, removing hike tail risk entirely.

macro_events.geographic_dimension: US Big Tech → Global semiconductor supply chain → Data center REITs
macro_events.historical_analog: Q1 2024 capex panic — similar fears, but earnings beat and Nasdaq rallied 15% over the following month.
macro_events.counterargument: Even if earnings beat, market may have priced in perfection at current valuations. MSFT at 25x forward, META at 22x — any guidance miss gets punished severely.
